chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Mahmud, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Drinking water whilst standing during the daytime nourishes the food, and drinking water whilst standing at nighttime causes the yellow water (jaundice).

key_terms.الْمَاءُ الْأَصْفَرُ: The yellow water — a classical Arabic medical term for jaundice or bilious disorders
key_terms.يُمْرِئُ: Makes palatable/digestible, aids the proper assimilation of food

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about drinking water while standing?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a prophylactic ruling on the proper manner of drinking water: consuming it standing up during the day aids digestion, whereas standing while drinking at night can lead to jaundice ('al-ma' al-asfar' — the yellow water). This hadith reflects the Imams' practice of combining religious guidance with practical medical advice that was comprehensible to the people of their time. The audience would have understood 'yellow water' (al-ma' al-asfar) as a reference to a recognised ailment involving yellowing of the body, corresponding to what modern medicine calls jaundice.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Bin Abu Mahmoud, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Drinking the water whilst standing at daytime nourishes the food, and drinking the water whilst standing at night time inherits the yellow water’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn abu Mahmud in a marfu‘ manner has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
During the day drinking water when standing makes the food more pleasant; but drinking water during the night when standing causes al-Safra ’ (yellowness, acidity).”’
